exposure: Race/ethnicity (non-Hispanic White, non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic Asian, Hispanic)
Maternal education level (less than high school graduate, high school graduate, college graduate, advanced degree)
outcome: Prevalence of low-risk nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex cesarean deliveries
cohort: Nulliparous women with term, singleton, vertex births from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention live births database (2016-2019)
finding: While higher levels of maternal education were associated with a lower likelihood of cesarean delivery, this protective effect varied among racial/ethnic groups, being smaller for non-Hispanic Black women and absent for Hispanic women.
mod_finding: This study examined racial and ethnic disparities in the prevalence of cesarean deliveries.
